newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia to set airport terminal bid, BA gets ok.
newsitem.headline: Latvia to set airport terminal bid, BA gets ok.

text.p: Latvia is expected to announce an international tender for the construction of a new passenger terminal at its Riga airport this year in a project worth $50 to $60 million, its transport minister said on Monday.
He also said that Latvia has told British Airways it can start flying to the Baltic state.
"We will start the new terminal as soon as the law on airport land is passed by the parliament in its final reading, expected in January," Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans told a news conference.
"We will have to introduce a departure tax to pay for the investment because the revenue earned by the airport will not cover it," Krishtopans added.
A new runway was built in 1995, helped with funds from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
Krishtopans said that in the six years since Latvia regained its independence from the former Soviet Union, Riga airport has become one of the most advanced in the ex-Communist bloc states.
Latvia is building a new terminal to cope with an expected increase in traffic as the country receives more international flights.
It is already serviced by three Western airlines and British Airways is expected to open a route in the summer.
Russian airlines Transaero and Aeroflot also fly to Riga as well as the Czech and Polish airlines.
Krishtopans welcomed BA's plans to start a flight to Riga and said it meant that it would give Latvia a higher profile in the international travel market.
